prompt: /knowledge-distiller TCP拥塞控制 I've been thinking about TCP congestion control. So basically TCP has this mechanism where it starts by sending like 1 packet, then 2, then 4 — doubling each time until there's a loss. That's slow start. When loss happens, it cuts in half and then starts increasing more slowly (additive increase). I think modern TCP uses something called cubic which is better for high-bandwidth networks because it uses a cubic function instead of linear. Also there's something called BBR from Google that's even better because it measures bandwidth instead of using loss. The whole point is to be fair to other connections. Is my understanding roughly right? Also I heard QUIC does all this at the application layer instead of in the kernel. Am I on the right track?
expected: 生成一篇聚焦 TCP 拥塞控制的中文 Obsidian 笔记，纠正慢启动、AIMD、CUBIC、BBR 与 QUIC 分层关系，保留证据与边界，不臆造链接。

expected: 生成一篇有因果主线的中文 Obsidian 笔记，区分表示、检索/排序、上下文导航与查询编排等轴线，说明每种方法修复的失败模式、代价与组合规则，而不是产品名词清单。
